title: The Pólya Insight: Fixed-Point Count = k^(number of orbits)
content: The key generalization from Burnside to Pólya is identifying **exactly** how many colorings each rotation fixes. For rotation by r on n positions: the orbit of position i is {j | j ≡ i mod gcd(r,n)}, giving gcd(r,n) orbits of size n/gcd(r,n) each. A coloring is fixed iff it's constant on each orbit, so there are k^gcd(r,n) fixed colorings. This follows from `ZMod.addOrderOf_coe`: the additive order of r in ZMod n is n/gcd(n,r), which is the orbit size.
mathContext: For $r \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$: the subgroup $\langle r \rangle = \{kr \bmod n \mid k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ has order $\text{addOrderOf}(r) = n/\gcd(n,r)$. Two positions $i,j$ are in the same orbit iff $i - j \in \langle r \rangle$ iff $\gcd(r,n) \mid (i-j)$ iff $i \equiv j \pmod{\gcd(r,n)}$. Hence $|\text{Fix}(r)| = k^{\gcd(r,n)}$.

title: addOrderOf_rotation: Orbit Size via ZMod.addOrderOf_coe
content: `addOrderOf_rotation` proves that the additive order of r in ZMod n is n/gcd(n, r.val). The proof uses `ZMod.natCast_zmod_val` to rewrite r as ↑r.val, then applies `ZMod.addOrderOf_coe` from Mathlib. This is the bridge between the orbit structure of cyclic rotation and Mathlib's number theory.
mathContext: Mathlib's `ZMod.addOrderOf_coe (a : ℕ) {n : ℕ} (n0 : n ≠ 0) : addOrderOf (↑a : ZMod n) = n / n.gcd a` combined with `ZMod.natCast_zmod_val : (r.val : ZMod n) = r` gives `addOrderOf r = n / Nat.gcd n r.val`. For $n=4$: orders are 1, 4, 2, 4 for $r = 0, 1, 2, 3$.

title: IsFixed: Computable Fixed-Coloring Predicate
content: `IsFixed n k r c` says coloring c : Fin n → Fin k is fixed by rotation r ∈ Fin n: every position i maps to the same color as position (i + n - r.val) mod n (the backward rotation). The `DecidablePred` instance uses `Fintype.decidableForallFintype`, enabling `native_decide` proofs for concrete fixed-point counts.
mathContext: For rotation r, the action sends position i to position i + r (mod n), so the backward rotation (undoing rotation r) sends i to i - r = (i + n - r) mod n. A coloring c is fixed iff c(i) = c(i - r) for all i.

title: fixed_factors_through_mod: Orbit Equality via Bezout
content: The key structural lemma: if A is fixed by rotation r, then positions i and j with i.val ≡ j.val (mod gcd(r,n)) satisfy c(i) = c(j). The proof has three steps: (1) show the backward step c(x+r) = c(x); (2) iterate to c(x + m*r) = c(x) for any m; (3) use Bezout's identity (Nat.gcd_eq_gcd_ab) to find m with (i + m*r) % n = j. The Bezout step converts 'same mod gcd' to 'reachable by rotation', which is the algebraic heart of the orbit characterization.
mathContext: Bezout: $\gcd(r,n) = r \cdot A + n \cdot B$ for integers $A, B$. If $\gcd(r,n) \mid (j-i)$, write $j - i = \gcd(r,n) \cdot C$, so $j - i = (r \cdot A + n \cdot B) \cdot C = r \cdot (AC) + n \cdot (BC)$. Thus $j \equiv i + r \cdot (AC) \pmod{n}$, i.e., $m = AC$ rotations carry $i$ to $j$.

title: polya_cyclic_fixed_count: Bijection |Fix(r)| = k^gcd(r,n)
content: Constructs the explicit bijection between {c : Fin n → Fin k // IsFixed n k r c} and (Fin d → Fin k) where d = gcd(r.val, n). The forward map sends a fixed coloring c to its restriction to the first d positions (Fin d representative). The backward map sends f to (i ↦ f ⟨i.val % d, ...⟩) — coloring by orbit representative. Right_inv is immediate (mod preserves Fin d values). Left_inv uses fixed_factors_through_mod to show that evaluating at orbit representatives agrees with the original coloring.
mathContext: Bijection: $c \mapsto (j \mapsto c(j))$ for $j < d$; inverse $f \mapsto (i \mapsto f(i \bmod d))$. Well-defined since $i \equiv i \bmod d \pmod{\gcd(r,n)}$, so $c(i) = c(i \bmod d)$ by fixed_factors_through_mod. Cardinality: $|\text{Fin}\,d \to \text{Fin}\,k| = k^d = k^{\gcd(r,n)}$.

title: Fixed-Point Counts for n=4 by native_decide
content: The four rotation-specific theorems are proved by `native_decide`, computing directly that: identity (r=0) fixes all 16 colorings; rotation by 1 fixes 2 (constant); rotation by 2 fixes 4 (period-2: c(0)=c(2), c(1)=c(3)); rotation by 3 fixes 2 (constant). These match k^gcd(r,n) = 2^gcd(r,4) for r=0,1,2,3.

title: Pólya Sum Formula: Two Equivalent Forms (Both Proved for n=4)
content: Two formulations of the Pólya sum are verified for n=4, k=2 by `native_decide`: (1) Σ_{r:Fin 4} 2^gcd(r,4) = 24; (2) Σ_{d|4} φ(4/d)·2^d = 24. Their equivalence is also proved. The general identity Σ_{r:Fin n} k^gcd(r,n) = Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d)·k^d holds because: for each divisor d|n, exactly φ(n/d) rotations r have gcd(r,n)=d (those with gcd(r/d, n/d)=1, i.e., r/d coprime to n/d).
mathContext: Reindexing: group rotations $r \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ by $d = \gcd(r,n)$. For each $d \mid n$, the number of $r$ with $\gcd(r,n) = d$ is $\varphi(n/d)$ (by Euler's totient: $\{r/d : \gcd(r/d, n/d) = 1\}$ has $\varphi(n/d)$ elements). Hence $\sum_r k^{\gcd(r,n)} = \sum_{d|n} \varphi(n/d) \cdot k^d$.

title: Fiber-Totient Bijection and Pólya Sum Identity
content: fiber_card_eq_totient proves that the fiber {r : Fin n | gcd(r.val, n) = d} has exactly φ(n/d) elements. The proof constructs a bijection r ↦ r.val/d with {s < n/d | Coprime(n/d, s)}: forward map divides by d (valid since d | r.val), injectivity uses linarith on d*(r1.val/d) = d*(r2.val/d), surjectivity sends s ↦ d*s. polya_sum_identity then uses Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to to reindex the rotation sum by divisors.
mathContext: $|\{r < n : \gcd(r,n) = d\}| = \varphi(n/d)$, via $r \mapsto r/d$ with $\{s < n/d : \gcd(s, n/d) = 1\}$. Hence $\sum_{r < n} k^{\gcd(r,n)} = \sum_{d \mid n} \varphi(n/d) \cdot k^d$.

title: Necklace Count and General Pólya Statement
content: polya_binary4_necklace_count derives 24/4 = 6 distinct binary necklaces of length 4 by combining polya_sum_Z4_binary with arithmetic. polya_necklace_formula_statement gives the general formula conditioned on Burnside's lemma and the fixed-point formula as hypotheses — a clean conditional statement of what PET achieves. The 6 necklace classes are: {0000}, {0001,0010,0100,1000}, {0011,0110,1100,1001}, {0101,1010}, {0111,1110,1101,1011}, {1111}.
mathContext: $\#\text{binary 4-necklaces} = \frac{1}{4}\sum_{r=0}^{3} 2^{\gcd(r,4)} = \frac{24}{4} = 6$. General: $n \cdot N_k(n) = \sum_{r < n} k^{\gcd(r,n)} = \sum_{d \mid n} \varphi(n/d) \cdot k^d$.
